notes: Converted from the retired classic Datalog-program benchmark collection (the 0428 wave).

Direct Lean semantic certificate: the kernel proves that the linear even/odd loop computes exactly the nonempty finite paths, whose union is transitive and is contained in every transitive pre-fixed-point bound. It has no external FOL assumptions or successful Vampire jobs.
title: Prefix-equivalence: naive all_paths_via_even_odd (linear) computes lfp of tc_nonlinear
explanation: The loop naively evaluates the all_paths_via_even_odd program (Tb the odd-length paths via Tb:=E∪(E∘Ta), Ta the even-length paths via Ta:=E∘Tb, and Tc:=Ta∪Tb their union), matching the linear all_paths_via_even_odd.dl program. The Hoare triple is the least-fixpoint introduction obligation for the non-linear transitive-closure program T(x,y):-E(x,y), T(x,y):-T(x,z),T(z,y): given any R that is already a pre-fixpoint of that non-linear program, the computed Tc must itself be a pre-fixpoint of it and lie below R, so the even/odd decomposition computes the (non-linear) transitive closure, since every path has odd or even length.
preInWords: The precondition states that R is a pre-fixpoint of the non-linear transitive-closure program: E ∪ (R∘R) ⊆ R.
postInWords: The postcondition states that the computed Tc is itself a pre-fixpoint of the non-linear transitive-closure program, E ∪ (Tc∘Tc) ⊆ Tc, and that Tc ⊆ R.

-- all_paths_via_even_odd_linear
-- Executed WHIEL program
OL(x,y) :- E(x,y).
OL(x,y) :- E(x,z), EL(z,y).
EL(x,y) :- E(x,z), OL(z,y).
T(x,y) :- EL(x,y).
T(x,y) :- OL(x,y).

tc(x, y) :- tc(x, z), tc(z, y).
